text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Face of poverty ever-changing: Study suggests huge number of Canadian go back and forth over low-income line.
- Bosnia concern overshadows NATO advance: Admission of Poland, Hungary and Czech Republic anticipated.
- Public-sector unions target Bill 136: CUPE leaders seek mandate to organize strike across Ontario in fall.
- Vote a signal to NAFTA partners: In demanding electoral freedoms, Mexicans serve notice they want to be consulted.
- Suspect charged in slaying of child: Man arrested after teen stabbed.
- Mergers on target for record: Consolidations and acquisitions of Canadian companies jump 21 percent in first half of '97.
- Marchi a new breed of trade minister: The former environment minister says putting social concerns alongside business matters will be his trademark.
- Laurentian stake brings Eaton's C$67.6 million: Sale could mean cash boost for retailer.
- Gold price freefall continues: Metal loses lustre as inflation hedge.
- Martin rebuffs move to ease 20 percent ceiling on RRSP foreign content.
- Millions wiped off gold stocks: Producers struggle to put best possible face on bullion's collapse.
